underwater_projection.classification: engineering estimate, not an in-water measurement
notes: 250 ksps is the converter and PL sample rate, not the usable acoustic bandwidth.
The 20 kHz occupied band assumes the transducer, matching network, amplifier, and hydrophone support 20–40 kHz.
Apply wideband Doppler resampling before OFDM frequency correction; one metre per second produces about 20 Hz shift at 30 kHz.
A narrower 10 kHz acoustic band roughly halves these payload estimates.
research_context: Socheleau et al. (2012) report 2–4 bit/s/Hz achievable on real underwater channels at 15–20 dB SNR under their modeled conditions.
Ebihara et al. (2018) measured up to 50 ms delay spread and 4.5 Hz Doppler spread in a mobile harbor experiment.
MinhHai et al. (2016) report 7.5 kbit/s over an 8 kHz band on a moving 30 m vertical link.
